text:
Predicates:
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(y, x) ::: y is located in x.
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
Donated(x) ::: x has been donated.
InRangeInTexas(x) ::: x is in a mountain range in Texas.
HasMineInRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range with a mine that has been donated.

Premises:
MountainRange(picuris) ∨ MountainRange(texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(juanDeOñate, picuris) ::: Juan de Oñate visited the Picuris Mountains.
Mine( HardingPegmatite) ∧ LocatedIn(HardingPegmatite, picuris) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine is located in the Picuris Mountains.
Donated(HardingPegmatite) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine was donated.
∀x (MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(y, x) ∧ HasMineInRange(x) → ∃z (Mine(z) ∧ Donated(z))) ::: In Texas, no mountain range with a mine that has been donated.

Conclusion:
¬LocatedIn(HardingPegmatite, texasmountain) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine is not located in a mountain range in New Mexico.
